title: Built a six-agent Grok trading desk for Robinhood. Goes live tomorrow with $500
author: GOATthings11
selftext:
I've been building AI agent systems for a while and finally pointed one at the market. It's six Grok bots, each with its own role: a Trading Lead, a Research Analyst, an X Scanner for catalysts and sentiment, a Risk Officer with veto power, an Execution Agent, and a Monitor & Report agent that sends me daily summaries.

Most of the work went into the rules. There are position sizing limits, a max daily loss that shuts everything down, mandatory stops, no averaging down, and caps on single-ticker exposure. The Risk Officer has the final word and the Trading Lead can't override it.

My thinking is that most retail losses come from discipline, not information. If you take the human out of execution, the rules actually get followed.    
I funded it with $500 to start, and it goes live tomorrow at the open. I'll try to remember to post results either way.

Has anyone here done something similar? I'd like to hear any feedback on agentic trading with Robinhood.

comments.author: Austin-Reed1
comments.body: oh interesting setup with the risk officer having veto power. i've seen a few people try multi agent setups on robinhood and the api rate limits usually become the bottleneck fast. grok has decent reasoning but the robinhood api doesnt give you websocket fills so your execution agent is polling. how are you handling the latency between the monitor agent seeing a fill and the risk officer recalculating exposure? also curious what you're using for the x scanner, official api or a wrapper? the $500 is smart for live testing but slippage on fractional shares at open will eat you alive on anything lower volume.

replies.author: GOATthings11
replies.body: So any proposal from the trading lead auto goes directly to the risk officer. Risk officer either vetoes or approves. If vetoed a report gets sent to the monitor and report (so the bots can continue to learn from each other on their Saturday regroup/strategy session etc). If approved risk routes to execution agent for trade. Execution agent sends the fill (day limit buys only) to monitor and report (checks every 30 min for changes with corresponding alerts set up) not trying to overload the apis on day one nor is it specifically for day trading, although it could be. 6% trailing stops. all types of safeguards in, whole shares only. X Scanner im not really sure yet tbh, it is giving me a list of trusted accounts in its first few runs, i only have it running in morning once that coincides with the market watcher - all points to the research analyst.

comments.author: Sea-Air-1781
comments.body: Yep I have been running something similair for 4 months. I have the team do Spy bull spreads based on$tick and RSI plus other metrics and a crypto trader along with the boss who trades for me so I take emotion out of it with option stop loss based on ATR etc. I also do an ORB style bot. I am up $600 roughly paper trading and some real money losses in this horrible choppy market plus the last 2 weeks with q's and spy falling.

comments.author: Ok_Map5721
comments.body:
Love that the Risk Officer has a real veto, most agent setups I see skip that part entirely. Starting at $500 is also the right size for this.

Main question though: what's the edge? I mean the actual reason the entries should make money. Did you backtest the Research Analyst and X Scanner signals before going live, and if so, what did they show after costs?

I ask because discipline stops you from blowing up, but it doesn't create an edge. My own bot followed its rules perfectly, every stop, every size limit, no exceptions, and it still lost steadily, because the entries themselves had no edge. Perfect execution of a coin flip is still a coin flip, just with fees.

A few things I'd set up before tomorrow's open, so the results actually tell you something:

1. Write down now what "working" means, e.g. beat buy-and-hold SPY over the same period after costs. Otherwise any result will feel like a signal.  
2. Log every decision, including the trades the Risk Officer vetoed and what they would have done. That's the most interesting data you'll get.  
3. Don't judge it on one month. With a handful of trades a week, you'll need a few hundred trades before luck and skill separate.

Please do post results either way, genuinely curious how the X Scanner does. Sentiment from X is the part I'd expect to be noisiest.

comments.author: Ok_Map5721
comments.body:
Since you're clearly building seriously, a separate ask: I'm actively looking for people to research with.

My situation is kind of the mirror of yours. My bot is honest. It doesn't bleed money, because it refuses to trade anything that doesn't pass, but it doesn't make money either. The plumbing works: data, execution, risk limits, and a testing pipeline that kills bad ideas. What's missing is something worth trading.

So I'm running an open brainstorm. Bring an idea, a market you think is still inefficient, a data source people ignore, even "here's why X can't work". I'll run the promising ones through the same brutal tests and post the results either way, so everyone learns. If something actually turns into money, I'm open to sharing with whoever brought the idea.

Only rule: no fairy tale sellers or shovel sellers. No courses, no signals, no tools for sale, ideas in the open only.
